test_title: SSC CGL Tier 2 Quant Previous Year Paper (Held On: 29 Jan 2022)
subject: general
question: One cup has juice and water in the ratio 5 ∶ 2, while another cup of the same capacity has them in the ratio 7 ∶ 4, respectively. If contents of both the cups (when full) are poured in a vessel, then what will be the final ratio of water to juice in the vessel?
solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Sum of ratio parts: Cup 1 = 5 + 2 = 7; Cup 2 = 7 + 4 = 11.

Make capacity equal by taking LCM of 7 and 11 = 77.

Cup 1 (multiply by 11): Juice = 55, Water = 22.

Cup 2 (multiply by 7): Juice = 49, Water = 28.

Total Water : Total Juice = (22 + 28) : (55 + 49) = 50 : 104 = 25 : 52.

**∴ The correct answer is 25 : 52.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Ratio of Juice : Water in Cup 1 = 5 : 2

Ratio of Juice : Water in Cup 2 = 7 : 4

Capacity of both cups is the same.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/6d12a4e2a6293f7806f855baa03e6392dfcb289dd51be4ede54e72ea72284f22.png] 

**Calculations:**

⇒ Total capacity = LCM(5+2, 7+4) = LCM(7, 11) = 77 units

⇒ Juice in Cup 1 = 5/7 × 77 = 55 units

⇒ Water in Cup 1 = 2/7 × 77 = 22 units

⇒ Juice in Cup 2 = 7/11 × 77 = 49 units

⇒ Water in Cup 2 = 4/11 × 77 = 28 units

⇒ Total Juice in vessel = 55 + 49 = 104 units

⇒ Total Water in vessel = 22 + 28 = 50 units

⇒ Required ratio (Water : Juice) = 50 : 104

⇒ Required ratio = 25 : 52

**∴ The correct answer is 25 : 52.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Mixture Equalization Rule

When mixing two or more mixtures of the same quantity, always equalize the sum of the ratio parts by using their LCM before adding the individual components.

Ratio Conversion

Always pay close attention to the final order requested (e.g., Water to Juice vs Juice to Water) as options often include the reciprocal ratio to confuse the solver.

Compound Ratio

If mixtures are mixed in different proportions (e.g., 2:3), first equalize the capacities and then multiply the ratios by the respective mixing proportions before adding.</p
